topic: Series RC and RL Circuits on AC
title: Series RC and RL Circuits Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
In the lab, Aarav's resistor shows 6 V and his capacitor shows 8 V on an AC supply of only 10 V. Why not 14? In this animated lesson two ropes pulling a box at right angles show the idea, and then we see how a resistor, a capacitor and an inductor each shift the current against the voltage on AC.

On a live breadboard the oscilloscope draws the resistor voltage, the capacitor voltage and the supply together: they add at every instant, but their peaks never line up. Swap the capacitor for a coil and the phase flips. We add voltages as phasors (arrows), build the impedance triangle, and get Z = √(R² + X²), tan φ = X/R and the power factor cos φ = R/Z for series RC (current leads) and series RL (current lags). Then a worked example (60 Ω and 80 Ω give Z = 100 Ω), the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 36 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 5: Application of D.C and A.C to Passive Components | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 7: Alternating Current | ISC Class 12 Physics: Alternating Current (L-R and C-R series circuits).
